contract: The coast plan (S3 of the engine design; replaces riven-shores.json). The coast comes in segments: coast sites sit on a jittered grid of cellBlocks (times the world's layout scale); a site within keepWithinCells cells of the coast is kept and moved onto the shore, the rest are dropped, and each column near the coast belongs to its nearest kept site, so segment edges cross the coast. A segment's type and band width are chosen once, at its site, from facts the land offers before any shore shaping, read probeBlocks inland of the site, each 0 to 1: low, middle, high and rugged (the land's level), cape, headland, shelter and shoaling (the outline's coast), grade (the broad slope across the shore between rockSlope's two values), rocky (grade or cape), wet (moisture above wetMoisture), warm (above warmCelsius) and bias (always 1). The type is the most suitable, each score shaken by up to choiceJitter so neighbouring segments vary; its band width and foot are drawn inside their ranges.

Each type shapes only its band, from the waterline inland: cliff and headland keep a foot of foot blocks at sea level, then rise to the inland ground within the first quarter of the band; bluff rises over the whole band from its foot; platform keeps a bench a block above the sea over 40% of the band, then rises over the next 20%; beach lays a berm two blocks above the sea over a quarter of the band, then rises gently; marsh stays a block above the sea over 70% of the band, then rises. Past the band the ground keeps its own height. Where two segments meet, their profiles blend over blendBlocks.

kind names what the type is to everything that reads the shore (cliff, rock, beach, marsh): a beach's berm is beach and the rest of its band coastal plain. The band's rise is the shore's land weight, which raising features read as their envelope: inside a band a feature may rise no higher than the sea plus the land weight times the highest surface (bent softly above kneeFraction of that room); past the band, without limit.

Forms (S3b, terrain-v110): a type lists its forms with perBlocks, the blocks of shore per slot. A segment places each form once, in slots along its shore around its site (cellBlocks wide, each jittered by slotJitter), moved exactly onto the shore and kept only on the segment's own stretch. CLIFF_PLATFORM, STEPPED_HEADLAND and JOINT_COVES are the MIT rocky kernels (contrib.rocky), tuned by families and coveDepth: their facts are the cliff top one and one and a half kernel widths inland, their drop is that cliff's own relief, exposure below minimumExposure fades them into sheltered water, and they only lower land, by the segment's share of each column, fading over the band's last fifth and never below a channel's levee. A STACK_ARCH slot is an arch (arch.fraction of slots) or a group of one to stack.groupMax stacks. A stack is a lobed, slightly elongated outline (radiusBlocks, elongation, lobes) centreBlocks out to sea, whose columns rise from the water at the outline to its height (heightBlocks, no taller than the cliff behind it) a taper's width in, under a rough top (roughness); companions are smaller and lower (companionScale, companionHeight) beside it along the shore. Every column of a stack's outline and of a 2-block moat must be open, supplied sea. An arch is a fin from landBlocks inside the cliff out to lengthBlocks at sea, halfThicknessBlocks thick (varying by thicknessVariation, wandering by wanderBlocks), lowering by seawardFall toward its end and across its crown, pierced by a half-ellipse rising from the water (openingCentre, openingWidth and openingHeight of its length and height, its rim roughened by irregularity) under at least roofBlocks of roof; its opening stands over open, supplied sea and its end in the sea. Stacks and arches build from each column's own ground. A SEA_CAVE is a tapering vault from one block above the water, lengthBlocks long (no longer than the band), halfWidthBlocks wide and heightBlocks high, cut no higher than roofBlocks under the column's surface; nearer the face, where that roof would be thinner, the column is cut down to the vault's floor, a notch through which the cave opens; neither opens an aquifer. Stacks and arches need exposed water at their shore point. Within a segment no stack, arch or sea cave overlaps another's body (the form listed first keeps its place), and a body claims only the columns it builds. Forms leave protected, wet and banked columns alone.

Sediment (S3b-2, terrain-v113): a type lists its sediment forms, the MIT sedimentary kernels (contrib.coast) tuned by sediment.tuning, and a segment places them once against the ground the coast forms left. Its stretch is the segment's own shore walked from its site both ways, guideBlocks a step along each point's own shore and snapped onto it, until a point belongs to another segment (that point is kept, so stretches overlap). A BEACH_BENCH follows the whole stretch. A SPIT grows, by spitChance, from each stretch end whose next point belongs to a cliff or rock kind, rooted 2 blocks inland and drifting away from the rock. A TOMBOLO ties a slot every tomboloSlotBlocks to the nearest stack seaward within 40 degrees of the normal, or else to the first land met seaward across open water when open sea surrounds it within isletRadiusBlocks (an islet, not a far shore), inside the kernel's tie bounds; a segment keeps one. The segment's type is the kernel's admission; a spit or tombolo stands only where every node of its line is unreserved and between the shoal's depth and a beach's height. Sediment leaves every column a coast form claimed alone; elsewhere a column takes the highest edit; deposition forms only build, a bench may cut the low shore, no edit lowers a channel's levee, and sand rising from marine columns is emergent.

Marsh (S3b-2, terrain-v114): MUD_FLAT and TIDAL_CREEK are Riven's own. A TIDAL_CREEK grows, by creek.chance, from a mouth every creek.slotBlocks along the stretch (a point clear of each owned end) where the sea four blocks out is open, supplied and unreserved at the water's top. Its first channel starts two blocks out to sea and runs inland along the shore's normal with the mouth's half width and depth, a node every stepBlocks wandering by up to wanderDegrees, within maximumTurnDegrees of its heading and spreadDegrees of inland, narrowing to tipHalfWidthBlocks and a block's depth over its length; a node may queue a branch (branchChance, at branchAngleDegrees to either side, scaled by branchScale, to orders levels and maximumChannels a creek), grown breadth first. A channel stops before a node whose column is not land under marshShare marsh within marshFlatRiseBlocks of the water's top, whose banks bankBlocks past either edge are neither open sea nor unreserved land at or above the water's top, or (past its first three steps) within bankBlocks of an earlier channel of the segment; a creek whose first channel takes fewer than three steps is dropped. A creek's unreserved land columns take its deepest bed, a block under the water's top at a channel's edge and its depth at its line, and the sea's water level, wet as a stream is: they stay land and keep the marsh's biome. MUD_FLAT covers, without changing height, every creek's bed and the flat of a type listing it (marshShare, within marshFlatRiseBlocks) where two octaves of value noise (mud.wavelengthBlocks) plus shoreBonus fading over shoreBlocks from the shore and creekBonus over creekBlocks from a creek's edge exceed threshold.
